content: The American Association of Homes and Services for the Aging (AAHSA) is an organization dedicated to supporting aging populations through housing and service initiatives. The American Association of Medical Colleges (AAMC) represents accredited medical schools and teaching hospitals in the United States, focusing on medical education and research. The Adjusted Average Per Capita Cost (AAPCC) is a metric used in healthcare to estimate the average cost of care per individual, adjusted for demographic and health factors. The American Association of Physicians and Surgeons (AAPS) is a professional organization advocating for the independence and integrity of medical practice. An Autologous Bone Marrow Transplant (ABMT) involves harvesting and reinfusing a patient’s own bone marrow, typically used in the treatment of certain cancers. The American Cancer Society (ACS) is a nationwide organization dedicated to cancer research, education, and advocacy for patients and survivors. The Administration for Children and Families (ACF) is a division of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services that provides programs to support child welfare and family stability. The American Dietetic Association (ADA) is a professional organization for dietitians and nutritionists, promoting evidence-based nutrition practices. The American Dental Association (ADA) is the leading professional association for dentists in the United States, focusing on oral health and dental care standards. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to diabetes research, education, and advocacy for individuals living with diabetes. The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) is a landmark civil rights law that prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities in all areas of public life. Activities of Daily Living (ADL) refer to basic self-care tasks such as eating, bathing, dressing, and mobility, often used as a measure of functional independence. An Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) is an unintended and harmful response to a medication, which may require medical intervention or discontinuation of the drug. The ADMIRAL study investigated the use of Abciximab prior to direct angioplasty and stenting in patients with myocardial infarction, focusing on both acute and long-term outcomes. Aid to Families with Dependent Children (AFDC) was a federal assistance program providing financial support to low-income families with children, replaced by TANF in 1996. The African Medical Association (AFMA) is a regional organization representing healthcare professionals across Africa, focusing on public health and medical education. The American Hospital Association (AHA) is a national organization representing hospitals and healthcare systems, advocating for quality care and healthcare policy. The American Heart Association (AHA) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to cardiovascular health through research, education, and advocacy. The American Health Care Association (AHCA) represents long-term care providers, including nursing homes and assisted living facilities, advocating for quality care. An Area Health Education Center (AHEC) is a program designed to improve healthcare access in underserved areas by training and supporting healthcare professionals. America’s Health Insurance Plans (AHIP) is a trade association representing the health insurance industry, focusing on policy advocacy and consumer education. The Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) is a federal agency tasked with improving the quality, safety, and efficiency of healthcare in the United States. The African Malaria Network Trust (AMANET) is an organization focused on malaria research and capacity building in Africa to combat the disease effectively. The American Medical Group Association (AMGA) represents medical groups and integrated healthcare systems, promoting high-quality, cost-effective care. The American Nurses Association (ANA) is a professional organization representing registered nurses, advocating for the nursing profession and patient care standards. The American Optometric Association (AOA) is the leading professional association for optometrists, focusing on eye health and vision care. The American Osteopathic Association (AOA) represents osteopathic physicians and promotes the practice of osteopathic medicine. The Administrative Procedures Act (APA) governs the process by which federal agencies develop and issue regulations, ensuring transparency and public participation. The American Psychiatric Association (APA) is a professional organization for psychiatrists, advancing mental health research, education, and clinical practice. The American Pharmaceutical Association (APA) is a professional organization representing pharmacists, focusing on medication management and patient safety. Ambulatory Payment Classification (APC) is a system used by Medicare to determine reimbursement rates for outpatient services. All Patient Diagnosis Related Groups (APDRG) is a classification system used to group patients with similar clinical conditions and resource needs. The American Public Health Association (APHA) is a professional organization dedicated to public health advocacy, education, and research. The American Protestant Hospital Association (APHA) represents faith-based hospitals, focusing on healthcare delivery and community service. The American Society of Anesthesiology (ASA) is a professional organization for anesthesiologists, promoting patient safety and the advancement of anesthesiology. An Ambulatory Surgery Center (ASC) is a facility where surgical procedures not requiring hospital admission are performed. An Administrative Service Organization (ASO) provides administrative support services, such as claims processing, for healthcare providers and insurers. Average Systolic Peak Velocity (ASPV) is a hemodynamic measurement used in cardiovascular assessments, particularly in echocardiography. The Association of State and Territorial Health Officials (ASTHO) represents public health agencies in the United States, focusing on health policy and practice. The Average Wholesale Price (AWP) is a benchmark used in the pharmaceutical industry to determine drug pricing and reimbursement rates.
